diagnosis.root_cause: In mv_npu_top, mat_ready is gated by can_accept_last_chunk (depends on hold_row_valid/pp_in_ready), introducing a combinational/progress dependency that can prevent final-chunk acceptance and stall matrix ingress indefinitely. This violates intended streaming progress and causes cocotb send_beat timeout on mat_ready before functional checking.

first_divergence.expected: mat_ready eventually asserts during COMPUTE_ROWS to accept matrix beats.
first_divergence.observed: Both tests fail with SimTimeoutError: timeout waiting mat_ready.

evidence.observation: Failure at line sending matrix beat: timeout waiting mat_ready at 1026ns.
evidence.relevance: First authoritative fatal failure in functional simulation.

evidence.observation: Same timeout waiting mat_ready at matrix send path.
evidence.relevance: Confirms systematic ingress deadlock, not data-specific mismatch.
Direct control condition that can block matrix acceptance based on downstream postproc readiness.

evidence.observation: Build/elaboration pass; only warnings (including latch inference) and no fatal compile errors.
evidence.relevance: Confirms primary failure is runtime protocol/progress, not compile legality.

alternative_hypotheses: Latch-inferred combinational temps in mv_npu_top/mv_mac16_core may cause X/unstable internal values but do not explain earliest mat_ready timeout as directly as gating deadlock.
DONE/out_xfer exit condition interplay in mv_ctrl_fsm could contribute to later completion issues after ingress deadlock is fixed.

repair_plan.recommended_change: Refactor top-level row-completion handoff so matrix ingress acceptance is not circularly blocked by postproc readiness. Specifically: (1) decouple mat_ready from immediate pp_in_ready on the last chunk by buffering completed row result in a registered pending slot, (2) drive pp_in_valid from that pending slot until accepted (lossless valid/ready behavior), and (3) only advance/clear pending row-result state on actual postproc acceptance while allowing matrix stream progress per FSM phase rules. Ensure no combinational latch behavior in this control block by assigning defaults on all paths.
do_not_change: Do not modify frozen tests or reference model.
Do not change architecture semantics, channel protocols, or top-level port list/widths.
Do not alter arithmetic definitions (INT8 multiply, INT32 wrap, optional bias/ReLU behavior).
Do not edit protected modules; keep fix localized to mv_npu_top integration/control sequencing.
expected_side_effects: mat_ready should assert and accept required matrix beats without timeout.
Row-result delivery to postproc becomes deterministic under backpressure.
After deadlock removal, any remaining value/timing mismatches may surface and must be checked in full regression.
